domanda: The International 10-20 System specifies the position of 19 electrodes on the scalp.
Frontopolar (Fp) electrodes are located in the parietal region of the scalp.
In a monopolar EEG recording, all channels share a single reference electrode.
In a monopolar EEG recording using all 19 electrodes of the 10-20 system, the total number of electrodes mounted on the subject's head (active + reference + ground) is 21.

An EEG study uses monopolar recording following the International 10-20 System, excluding all frontopolar (Fp) and occipital (O) channels (2 of each). The reference is a common linked mastoid pair (left + right mastoid). How many active EEG channels are recorded?

An EEG study records 15 active channels in monopolar configuration, using a common linked mastoid reference (left + right mastoid electrodes) and one ground electrode. How many total electrodes must be mounted on the subject's head?
Only the following four bipolar EEG channels are recorded: T7-C3, C3-Cz, Cz-C4, C4-T8. One ground electrode is required. How many electrodes must be mounted on the subject's head in total?
In a bipolar EEG chain T7-C3, C3-Cz, Cz-C4, C4-T8, the electrode C3 serves as both the negative input of one channel and the positive input of the next.
The Nyquist frequency is equal to half the sampling frequency.
Shannon's theorem requires that the analog signal contains no frequency components above the Nyquist frequency for correct reconstruction.
An anti-aliasing filter must have its cutoff frequency below the Nyquist frequency to prevent aliasing.
Aliasing is reversible: once a signal is aliased, it can be recovered by digital filtering.
An EEG system samples at 400 samples/s. The analog low-pass filter is set at 300 Hz. Is there an anti-aliasing problem, and why?
risposta: Yes — the filter cutoff (300 Hz) exceeds the Nyquist frequency (200 Hz)
opzione_b: No — 300 Hz is well below the sampling rate of 400 Hz
opzione_c: Yes — the sampling rate is too high for EEG
opzione_d: No — anti-aliasing filters are optional for EEG

domanda: An EMG system samples at 5000 samples/s and applies a bandpass filter 10–2000 Hz. Is there an anti-aliasing problem?
risposta: No — the filter upper cutoff (2000 Hz) is below the Nyquist frequency (2500 Hz)
opzione_b: Yes — the filter cutoff exceeds the Nyquist frequency
opzione_c: Yes — the lower cutoff introduces aliasing
opzione_d: No — EMG does not require anti-aliasing

domanda: A BCI system samples EEG at 100 Hz. To preserve beta-band activity (~13–30 Hz) while preventing aliasing despite a finite filter roll-off, what anti-alias corner frequency is most appropriate?
An sEMG system samples at 200 samples/s and uses an analog low-pass filter at 450 Hz. What is the consequence?
risposta: Aliasing: frequencies between 100 Hz and 450 Hz will fold into the signal band
opzione_b: No problem: 450 Hz is a standard EMG filter cutoff

domanda: An EEG system uses a 128 Hz sampling rate and an analog low-pass filter at 85 Hz. This setup causes aliasing because 85 Hz exceeds the Nyquist frequency of 64 Hz.
A system has sampling frequency fs = 128 Hz. What is the Nyquist frequency?
An ADC has a full-scale input range of V_range and N bits of resolution. Write the formula for the quantization step size V_LSB.
An 8-bit ADC has an input range of ±2.5 V (full-scale range = 5 V). What is the quantization step size V_LSB?
A 12-bit ADC has an input range of ±1.5 V (full-scale range = 3 V). What is the quantization step size V_LSB?
A 16-bit ADC has an input range of 10 V. What is the quantization step size V_LSB?
Quantization noise RMS equals V_LSB / sqrt(12).
The CMRR of a differential amplifier is defined as the ratio of the differential gain to the common-mode gain, expressed in dB.
A higher CMRR means the amplifier is better at rejecting common-mode interference such as powerline noise.
The input impedance of a biosignal amplifier should be much lower than the electrode contact impedance.
Given a differential gain A_D (dB) and a CMRR (dB), write the formula for the common-mode gain A_CM in dB.
risposta: A_CM = A_D - CMRR | A_{CM}[\text{dB}] = A_D[\text{dB}] - CMRR[\text{dB}]

(Hint: A_CM[dB] = A_D[dB] − CMRR[dB]; then output = A_CM × input_amplitude)
A biosignal amplifier has a differential gain of 60 dB (A_D = 1000) and CMRR = 110 dB. The common-mode gain A_CM in linear scale is approximately:
Electrode contact impedances should be low (ideally below 5–10 kΩ) to maximise the voltage delivered to the amplifier input.
The Motor-Related Cortical Potential (MRCP) is a slow negative EEG deflection that begins before voluntary movement onset.
The MRCP is typically maximal over the contralateral sensorimotor cortex relative to the moving limb.
Synchronized averaging of EEG trials reduces the amplitude of the evoked potential while keeping the noise constant.
The residual spontaneous EEG noise after averaging N trials has an amplitude equal to sigma_trial / sqrt(N).
After averaging N EEG trials, each with spontaneous EEG RMS amplitude σ, write the formula for the residual noise RMS in the average.
A motor task EEG study consists of 4 runs × 40 trials = 160 trials. The single-trial EEG RMS on a channel is 25 µV. What is the expected residual noise amplitude in the MRCP average?

In an MRCP experiment, the EEG epoch is defined as 8 s (4 s before and 4 s after movement onset), and EMG onset is used as time zero. The MRCP onset (as shown in Figure 1 of the Jun 2022 even exam) occurs 3 s before EMG onset. What is the MRCP onset latency relative to EMG onset?
In the same MRCP figure, the MRCP peak occurs 1 s after EMG onset. What is the MRCP peak latency relative to EMG onset?
A motor task involves right-arm shoulder flexion and elbow extension. On which EEG channel is the MRCP most likely to be maximal?
Cognitive planning time in an MRCP study is defined as the duration between MRCP onset and EMG onset.
MRCP amplitude is used as an index of cognitive effort level in the MRCP paradigm.
Two rest EEG runs have been mislabelled (eyes open vs eyes closed). How can they be distinguished?
risposta: Eyes-closed shows increased alpha rhythm amplitude on parieto-occipital channels
opzione_d: They cannot be distinguished without task events

domanda: The alpha rhythm (8–13 Hz) is typically suppressed (desynchronized) when the eyes are closed.
The mu rhythm has the same frequency range as the alpha rhythm but originates from the sensorimotor cortex.
Event-Related Desynchronization (ERD) of the mu rhythm occurs over the contralateral motor cortex when a hand movement is imagined.
Blink artifacts produce slow drifts below 0.5 Hz on frontal EEG channels.
Blink artifacts appear primarily on frontal EEG channels as large-amplitude transient deflections lasting a few hundred milliseconds.
Sweating artifacts produce very slow (below 0.5 Hz) and very large (up to several mV) drifts in the EEG baseline.
EMG artifacts contaminate primarily the delta band (1–4 Hz) of the EEG.
Powerline interference at 50 Hz should be removed using a notch filter rather than by rejecting contaminated trials.
In a monopolar recording, electrode O1 is located in the occipital region.
If electrode O1 produces popping artifacts but all other channels are clean, the correct approach is to reject only the O1 channel, not all trials.
A technician rejects all 160 trials because 55 of them show an electrode-popping artifact on a single channel (O1). What would have been the better approach?
risposta: Reject only the O1 channel and keep all 160 trials
opzione_b: Reject the 55 contaminated trials and keep 105
opzione_c: Apply a high-pass filter to remove the artifact
opzione_d: Apply a notch filter at the artifact frequency

domanda: During a motor imagery experiment, the mu rhythm desynchronizes when right-hand movement is imagined. On which electrode should this be most visible?
The frequency resolution of a periodogram is inversely proportional to the window length.
Welch's method (averaged periodogram) improves the variance of the spectral estimate at the cost of frequency resolution.
To achieve a frequency resolution of 0.5 Hz, the epoch/window length must be at least 2 seconds.
To achieve a frequency resolution of 2 Hz, the window length must be at least 500 ms.
Write the formula for the frequency resolution Δf of a periodogram as a function of the window length T_w.

A 32-channel EEG is recorded for 30 seconds at 200 samples/s. The analysis requires a frequency resolution of at least 0.5 Hz. Which spectral estimation method is most appropriate, and what minimum window/epoch length is required?
opzione_b: Single FFT on the full 30 s recording; no windowing needed

domanda: A BCI system requires Δf = 2 Hz in the PSD. The sampling rate is 100 Hz. What is the required window length in samples?
In a Welch PSD computation, the window length is 500 ms and the window shift (update interval) is 100 ms. What is the window overlap percentage?
Write the formula for window overlap percentage given window length T_w and window shift T_s.
A 4-second EEG trial is processed with a Welch PSD using 500 ms windows and 100 ms window shift. How many periodograms are averaged?
Write the formula for the number of Welch periodograms given trial duration T_trial, window length T_w, and shift T_s (assume the last window fits exactly).
A BCI uses 2 EEG channels (C3, C4) and extracts features from 8–30 Hz with 2 Hz frequency bins. What is the total length of the feature vector passed to the classifier?
Ordinary Coherence is a symmetric measure: Cxy(f) = Cyx(f).
Ordinary Coherence is a measure of directed causality between two signals.
The Granger Causality Test is a spectral measure defined in the frequency domain.
Partial Directed Coherence (PDC) is a spectral and directional measure of causality.
PDC is a bivariate method based on two-signal autoregressive models.
The Granger Test is preferred over PDC when data segments are short, because it requires fewer parameters to estimate.
A bivariate connectivity measure is susceptible to the hidden (common) source problem.
Using PDC completely solves the hidden source problem.
Using a different connectivity estimator for the PRE and POST sessions of an experiment introduces a methodological error.
A researcher wants to measure directed functional connectivity at specific frequency bands. The recording is short (limited data). Which estimator is most appropriate?
risposta: PDC (Partial Directed Coherence) — directional and spectral, but check data length
opzione_c: Granger Test — directional but not spectral

domanda: A study aims to analyse directed causality in EEG but only short recordings are available. Which connectivity estimator is the best compromise?
risposta: Granger Test — directional, does not require long data segments
opzione_b: PDC — multivariate but requires long recordings

domanda: Researchers use Ordinary Coherence for a PRE session and the Granger Test for a POST session to compare a rehabilitation effect. What is the main methodological problem?
risposta: The two methods measure different things (coherence vs causality; undirected vs directed), making the comparison invalid
opzione_b: Both methods are equivalent because they both quantify signal relationships
opzione_c: The problem is only the different data lengths, not the choice of estimator
opzione_d: There is no problem if the same threshold is applied to both

domanda: Which connectivity estimator is both directed (causality) AND spectral (frequency-resolved) AND multivariate?
Global Efficiency is defined as the average of 1/d_ij over all pairs of distinct nodes i≠j, normalised by N(N-1).
When two nodes are not connected by any path, the distance d_ij is infinite and their contribution to Global Efficiency is zero.
Global Efficiency ranges between 0 and 1.
A network with higher Global Efficiency always has more edges than a network with lower Global Efficiency.
Divisibility D ranges between 0 and 1 (exclusive of 0).
Modularity Q can take negative values.
In a directed graph, in-degree of node i equals the sum of column i of the adjacency matrix.
Write the formula for Global Efficiency E_g of a graph with N nodes and shortest-path distance matrix D (entries d_ij).
Write the formula for Divisibility D of a network with L total directed edges, given a partition where S edges connect nodes in different classes.

A directed network has 5 nodes. The distance matrix (diagonal = −, off-diagonal finite or ∞) has the following non-infinite entries summing to: 1/1+1/2+1/2+1/1+1/1+1/3+1/1+1/2 = 8. [N=5, N(N-1)=20]. What is the Global Efficiency?

A directed network has N=5 nodes, L=8 connections (PRE session). After rehabilitation (POST session), the network still has L=8 connections but the Global Efficiency increases from 0.40 to 0.66. What does this indicate?
risposta: The network reorganised: communication is more efficient despite the same number of connections
opzione_b: The number of connections increased from 8 to 11
opzione_c: The network density decreased after rehabilitation
opzione_d: Global Efficiency cannot change if the number of edges is constant

domanda: A network has N=8 nodes, L=13 directed edges, and a partition Ca=[1,1,1,1,2,2,2,2]. There are 0 edges between nodes of class 1 and class 2. What is the Divisibility D?
The same network (N=8, L=13) with a different partition Cb=[1,1,2,2,2,2,1,1] has 2 cross-class edges (S=2). What is the Divisibility D?

In a two-brain collaboration experiment, partition Ca assigns each brain to a separate class. Partition Cb assigns homologous regions of both brains to the same class. D and Q are higher for Cb than Ca. What does this tell us?
risposta: The two brains influence each other: homologous regions across subjects are more connected than within-brain regions
opzione_b: The two brains work completely independently
opzione_c: Ca is the correct partition and Cb introduces bias
opzione_d: Nothing can be concluded about inter-brain coupling from D and Q

domanda: Stereo EEG (sEEG) is the most appropriate intracranial recording technique for accessing deep subcortical structures.
ECoG (Electrocorticography) is suitable for recording from deep subcortical nuclei.
Scalp EEG has sufficient spatial resolution to distinguish activity in subcortical nuclei a few mm apart.
sEEG requires electrode implantation through the skull and brain parenchyma.

A study requires intracranial recordings from multiple subcortical regions (thalamus, basal ganglia) immediately before and after brain surgery in a patient. Which recording technique is most appropriate?
opzione_d: Local Field Potentials via surface grid

domanda: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates ECoG from sEEG?
risposta: ECoG records from the cortical surface via electrode grids; sEEG records from deep structures via stereotactically implanted depth electrodes
opzione_b: ECoG records from subcortical structures; sEEG records only from the cortex
opzione_c: ECoG and sEEG are equivalent in spatial resolution
opzione_d: sEEG requires a craniotomy while ECoG uses a burr hole

domanda: A bipolar sEMG recording from a single muscle requires exactly 3 electrodes: 2 differential inputs + 1 ground.
Two independent bipolar sEMG channels (on two different muscles) require 5 electrodes total: 4 recording + 1 shared ground.
A prosthetic control system uses 2 independent bipolar sEMG channels placed on different muscles, plus one shared ground electrode for the subject. How many sEMG electrodes are required in total?
The double-threshold EMG onset detection algorithm declares an onset only when the signal crosses an amplitude threshold AND remains above it for a minimum duration.
A false alarm in double-threshold onset detection occurs when the amplitude threshold is exceeded but the duration criterion is not met.

An sEMG envelope is monitored with a double-threshold algorithm: amplitude threshold A_c = 15 µV, duration criterion t_c = 60 ms. The signal crosses 15 µV at t = 400 ms but returns below threshold at t = 440 ms (duration = 40 ms < 60 ms). Then it crosses again at t = 590 ms and stays above for 80 ms. At what time is a valid onset declared?
risposta: 590 ms (first valid crossing meeting both criteria)

domanda: A moving average filter is applied to a rectified sEMG signal with a 250 ms window. If the window is shortened to 100 ms, how does the standard deviation of the output signal change?
risposta: Increases — less averaging means more variability in the output
opzione_b: Decreases — shorter window reacts faster and is smoother
opzione_c: No change — standard deviation depends only on the input signal
opzione_d: Decreases — fewer samples means less noise

domanda: A moving average filter is applied to sEMG with a 250 ms window. If the window is extended to 500 ms, how does the standard deviation of the output signal change?
risposta: Decreases — more averaging smooths the signal
opzione_b: Increases — longer window captures more noise
opzione_d: Increases — more samples means more variance

domanda: A moving average filter is an IIR filter because its output depends on past output samples.
A moving average filter is an FIR filter because its output is a weighted sum of a finite number of past input samples.
The Stimulus Onset Asynchrony (SOA) is the time between the onset of one stimulus and the onset of the next.
The Inter-Stimulus Interval (ISI) is the time between the end of one stimulus and the onset of the next.
ISI = SOA + stimulus duration.
Write the formula for ISI given SOA and stimulus duration T_stim.
risposta: ISI = SOA - T_stim | ISI = SOA - T_{stim}

domanda: A P300 experiment presents auditory tones with SOA = 1500 ms and each stimulus lasts 50 ms. What is the Inter-Stimulus Interval (ISI)?

In a P300 BCI experiment, the EEG is recorded from electrode Cz with reference electrodes A1 and A2 (left and right earlobes), plus one ground electrode. How many electrodes are placed on the subject in total?
The RMS value of a sinusoid with peak amplitude A is A / sqrt(2).
If two independent zero-mean signals have RMS values n1 and n2, the RMS of their sum is sqrt(n1² + n2²).
If two independent zero-mean signals have variances σ1² and σ2², the variance of their sum is σ1² × σ2².
Write the formula for the combined RMS of two independent zero-mean signals with individual RMS values n_1 and n_2.
Write the formula for the RMS of a sinusoid with peak amplitude A.
An EEG amplifier has differential gain A_D = 80 dB (= 10^4 linear). The input EEG RMS is 15 µV. What is the amplified EEG RMS at the output?

The same amplifier has CMRR = 90 dB. A 50 Hz common-mode interference has amplitude 150 mV at the input. The common-mode gain A_CM = A_D − CMRR = −10 dB ≈ 0.316 in linear scale. What is the approximate RMS of the residual 50 Hz artifact at the output? (RMS of sinusoid = peak / sqrt(2))
Using the two independent noise sources above (amplified EEG RMS = 150 mV; artifact RMS ≈ 33.5 mV), what is the total combined RMS noise at the ADC input?
Would a high-pass filter with a cutoff frequency of 30 Hz significantly affect the amplitude of P300 ERPs?
In a visual P300 oddball paradigm, if you increase the probability of target 'X' stimuli from 20% to 80% to get more trials, what happens to the P300 amplitude?
risposta: It decreases or disappears entirely because the brain no longer treats it as a rare event
opzione_c: It quadruples because there are four times as many target trials
opzione_d: It remains exactly the same because P300 is purely stimulus-driven
opzione_e: It increases because the subject has to pay more attention

domanda: Which recording technique is most indicated when the brain regions to be monitored in a pre-surgery study are all subcortical?
According to Pfurtscheller's classical 1999 algorithm, what is the correct sequence of steps for estimating ERD/S?
risposta: Segmentation -> Bandpass filtering -> Squaring -> Averaging -> Normalization
opzione_c: Bandpass filtering -> Segmentation -> Averaging -> Squaring -> Normalization
opzione_d: Segmentation -> Squaring -> Bandpass filtering -> Averaging -> Normalization
opzione_e: Bandpass filtering -> Averaging -> Normalization -> Segmentation -> Squaring

domanda: Which of the following is a necessary condition to successfully apply the Common Average Reference (CAR) to a dataset?
risposta: The signals must be acquired using a monopolar montage
opzione_c: The signals must be acquired using a bipolar longitudinal montage
opzione_d: The sampling frequency must be at least 1000 Hz
opzione_e: The high-pass filter must be set above 30 Hz

domanda: A 3-second EEG epoch is analyzed with a Welch PSD using 500 ms windows and 50% overlap. How many segments (M) are extracted?
Write the formula for calculating the shift step T_shift in Welch's algorithm as a function of the window length T_win and the fractional overlap O.
"risposta_alternativa": Tshift = Twin * (1 - O) | Tshift = Twin * (1 - overlap)

domanda: When analyzing sensorimotor rhythms (SMR) in the alpha and beta bands (8-30 Hz), which of the following artifacts must be REJECTED because its frequency spectrum directly overlaps with the interest band?

A P300 session has 4 runs separated by 3 breaks of 5 minutes each. Each run has 30 trials. Each trial lasts 7 s, and the inter-trial interval (ITI) is 1.5 s. What is the total duration of the session?
In the primary visual cortex, a far-tuned neuron is characterized by a tuning curve that responds mainly to:
opzione_d: Zero retinal disparity only (point of fixation)

The Blackman-Harris window is preferred over the rectangular window when the spectral components of interest are very closely spaced near the resolution limit, because of its narrow main lobe.
A plain periodogram with no windowing shows a spectral resolution df of 0.1 Hz. What was the duration (T) of the time-domain signal used for the calculation?
The Common Average Reference (CAR) approximation to an 'ideal' reference at infinity improves as the number of electrodes increases.
A BCI system records 8 channels. Each epoch contains 128 samples (corresponding to a 0.5 s SOA at 256 Hz). What is the length of the raw feature vector passed to the classifier?
Being a pairwise (bivariate) estimator, Ordinary Coherence is highly vulnerable to the common source problem, which can lead to spurious connections.
In graph theory, Local Efficiency (El) is defined as:
risposta: The average of the global efficiencies calculated on the local subgraphs of each node
opzione_c: The length of the shortest path between a node and its nearest neighbor
opzione_d: The fraction of present triangles over all possible triplets
opzione_e: The sum of in-degree and out-degree for a specific node

domanda: Write the formula for the Divisibility (D) of a network partition with total edges L and cross-class edges L_inter.
"risposta_alternativa": D = L / (L + Linter) | D = L / (L + S)

domanda: Write the formula for the Granger Causality Index G_y->x, where V_x|x is the univariate prediction error variance and V_x|x,y is the bivariate prediction error variance.
A modularity value Q equal to -0.19 indicates that the network:
risposta: Has fewer intra-community links than expected by chance, showing a non-modular structure
opzione_c: Has a perfectly modular structure with strong community segregation
opzione_d: Is completely disconnected with no active paths

The ERD/S (Event-Related Desynchronization/Synchronization) measures the amplitude of the phase-locked brain activity evoked by a stimulus.
Sweating artifacts are slow potentials with frequency components usually below 0.5 Hz, meaning they do not directly overlap with sensorimotor rhythms (8-30 Hz).
La variazione grezza dell'ampiezza sEMG espressa in millivolt può essere confrontata direttamente tra soggetti diversi senza opportuna normalizzazione.
In a multivariate autoregressive (MVAR) model of order p on N channels, the number of parameters to be estimated scales quadratically with the number of channels as p*N^2.
An acquisition system has fs = 256 Hz and applies an analog anti-aliasing filter at 200 Hz. Is this setup correct?
risposta: No — the filter cutoff (200 Hz) exceeds the Nyquist frequency (128 Hz), causing aliasing
opzione_c: Yes — the filter cutoff is below the sampling frequency (256 Hz)
opzione_d: No — anti-aliasing filters must be digital, not analog
opzione_e: Yes — 200 Hz is a standard cutoff for subcortical EEG

domanda: Which neuron orientation relative to the cortical surface is ideal for generating dipole fields that can summate and propagate to the scalp?
opzione_d: Radial orientation pointing outwards in all directions
